resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy (CCO)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough Zoning Official (Frank Sacco, Zoning/Code Enforcement Official)
requirements: Property must meet the Borough Property Maintenance Code (Chapter 151)
Rental units: a current CCO must be attached to the Borough landlord registration (Chapter 152)

fees.label: Certificate of continued occupancy
fees.quote: The fee for a certificate of continued occupancy, as per Chapter 151, Property Maintenance, shall be $25.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Contact the Borough Zoning Official, Frank Sacco, at Borough Hall (1700 Rt 54, Folsom, NJ 08037) to request the certificate of continued occupancy and pay the $25 fee. He holds office hours Mondays 5:00 to 7:00 PM. The Borough code does not publish a form, a lead time or the exact sale trigger, so call ahead to confirm.

The term on the lease and a copy of the current continued certificate of occupancy (CCO).

evidence.quote: Frank Sacco - Zoning Officer Email the Zoning Officer Office hours – Mondays 5:00 – 7:00 PM

resale_co.notes: Folsom's code (Section 103-3, re-read 2026-10-06) sets a $25 fee for a certificate of continued occupancy, handled by the Zoning Official, and Chapter 152 requires a current CCO for every registered rental. Chapter 151 (Property Maintenance, re-read 2026-10-06) does not spell out when a CCO is triggered on a sale, so we list it as required and tell buyers and sellers to confirm with the Zoning Official. Construction code work is done by the State DCA Construction Office, which is not the CCO issuer. Smoke/CO certificates come from the State (see fire section).

requirements: Smoke alarms, carbon monoxide alarms and, for homes with solar, generators or batteries, a secondary power source identification label (the State application is now the CSACMASPSIL)

authorities.name: NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement
authorities.lead_time: More than 10 business days before the change of occupant for the lowest fee

fees.label: Requested 4 to 10 business days before the change of occupant

fees.label: Requested fewer than 4 business days before the change of occupant
fees.quote: Requests for a CSACMAPFEC received fewer than four business days prior to the change of occupant: $161.00

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply online through the NJ DCA Fire Safety portal (Apply Smoke Certification), as the Borough's Construction Office page directs. Pay online before submitting; a valid email address is required. For help email BFCECodeAdmin@dca.nj.gov or call 609-633-6132.

fire_cert.notes: NJ DCA lists Folsom as State enforced (S) and its July 17, 2026 list marks it 'SC' (the State issues smoke certificates). The Borough's Construction Office page links sellers to the State Fire Safety portal. Fees are the State fees under N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d) ($45 / $90 / $161), now cited from the NJ Register adoption text instead of the State portal page. The directory lists (609) 633-6132; the Bureau's page lists (609) 633-6106 for Louis Kilmer. BFCECodeAdmin@dca.nj.gov is the State help address for residential smoke certificate questions.

open_questions: Is the $25 certificate of continued occupancy required on every 1-2 family sale, or only for rentals? The code sets the fee but does not state the sale trigger; confirm with the Zoning/Code Enforcement Official or the Borough Clerk at (609) 561-3178.
